question: Buds produced in the notches along the leaf margin of Bryophyllum fall on the soil and develop into new plants. Such a mode of reproduction is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**vegetative propagation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vegetative propagation** is a form of asexual reproduction in which new plants grow from parts of the parent plant, such as leaves, stems, and roots.
 
• In **Bryophyllum**, buds produced in the notches along the leaf margin fall on the soil and develop into new plants.
 
• This method allows for the rapid multiplication and reproduction of plants without the need for seeds.
 
• Vegetative propagation is commonly used in horticulture and agriculture to propagate plants with desirable traits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budding:**

 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• Commonly seen in yeast and some invertebrates like hydra.
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation:**
 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction where an organism splits into fragments, and each fragment develops into a new organism.
 
• Common in algae, fungi, and some plants.
 
 
 
• **Regeneration:**
 
 
• The process of renewal, restoration, and growth that makes genomes, cells, organisms, and ecosystems resilient to natural fluctuations or events that cause disturbance or damage.
 
• Seen in organisms like starfish, which can regrow lost arms.
 
 
 
• **Other Examples of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• Examples include the propagation of potatoes through tubers and strawberries through runners.
 
• This method is also used to propagate plants like sugarcane, ginger, and garlic.
